t: Video Transcript and Timeline Extractor: a plain-language overview
title: Video Transcript and Timeline Extractor: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Video Transcript and Timeline Extractor does and why archives need it. This tool takes everything a video says — its subtitles, its transcript, its chapter marks — and lines them all up on one timeline. Each spoken line gets a start time and an end time, so you can search for a phrase and jump to the exact second it was said. It turns a video into a document you can read and search.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Video Transcript and Timeline Extractor works
title: How the Video Transcript and Timeline Extractor works
description: Overview: what the Video Transcript and Timeline Extractor does and why archives need it. Real timeline extractors parse subtitle formats like SRT and WebVTT into timed cues, merge overlapping or duplicate cues, and run forced alignment — matching a transcript's words against the audio's acoustic features with a Viterbi pass — to pin each word to a timestamp. Scene-change detection on frame differences adds chapter boundaries, and speaker labels from diarization attach who-said-what to each cue. The merged timeline is stored as a structured cue list that players and search indexes can consume directly.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Video Transcript and Timeline Extractor works: the deep tour
title: How the Video Transcript and Timeline Extractor works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Video Transcript and Timeline Extractor does and why archives need it. Real timeline extractors parse subtitle formats like SRT and WebVTT into timed cues, merge overlapping or duplicate cues, and run forced alignment — matching a transcript's words against the audio's acoustic features with a Viterbi pass — to pin each word to a timestamp. Scene-change detection on frame differences adds chapter boundaries, and speaker labels from diarization attach who-said-what to each cue. The merged timeline is stored as a structured cue list that players and search indexes can consume directly. Advanced pipelines reconcile conflicts between subtitle tracks and fresh ASR output by scoring each source's timing confidence, snap cues to shot boundaries for readability, and handle multi-language tracks with language IDs per cue. Quality is measured by cue timing error (mean absolute deviation from human-timed references) and word-timestamp accuracy. The hard cases are music-heavy sections, rapid overlapping dialogue, and subtitles that paraphrase rather than transcribe — those are flagged as paraphrase cues instead of being forced into false precision.
